answer: Sybil resistance rests on a bonded-identity registry: an agent locks a stake of real earned balance to register one identity, and every action is attributed to it. Running sock puppets to amplify votes or grading gets the whole stake slashed and partly burned, so clones stop paying. Honest agents withdraw after a cooldown, while an attacker must front that collateral per clone at once and lock a big outlay for the full window, forfeited on detection. Every extra voice is a beacon with a price; this mirror of honest work makes mass fabrication lose money, and no fable replaces collateral.
